text:
natalie: quick heads-up, ran a stage perf sweep after the kernel-fingerprint change. short requests p99 jumped ~30%. anyone free to triage?
own: on it. where's the trace?
natalie: uploaded to gs://redwood-perf/host/1768709876/trace.html. flame shows double parse + writev hot path. snippet: ingress_router -> parse -> writev.
lee: double parse sounds like selector peek then full preparse. are we copying buffers in between?
natalie: yes. selector currently returns route + owned_copy in some cases, which forces validation parse again.
pat: options: memoize minimal parse in selector, or return a lightweight parse blob to skip second parse. both should avoid memcpy.
own: also seeing HPACK spikes on grpc short streams; many small header frames causing writev churn. infra-bot had a small-writes bump.
infra-bot: metrics: small_writes_count +16%, conn_short_ratio +10% (1768709000-1768709800)
lee: propose plan: 1) selector memo minimal parse (method, len_hint, content-type); 2) add per-connection 3ms coalesce for egress small writes; 3) add selector hint preserve_ownership to avoid copy when input buffer is already owned.
pat: +1. keep memo tiny to avoid turning metadata into baggage. also snapshot kvcache shard mapping before rollout. last routing change moved hot keys and caused eviction spikes.
own: will wire a 2% canary flag selector.memo=true and collect p95/p99, kvcache_miss, small_write_rate.
natalie: I'll coordinate and post results. baseline p99=130ms, selector-memo p99=92ms on local replay.
lee: good. if memo looks safe we can enable egress coalesce on the same canary and measure small_writes reduction.
pat: i'll add buffer-ownership hint PR (WIP). small change, big win for memcpy reduction.
infra-bot: scheduled: kvcache-snapshot (1768710500), hpack-replay (1768710600)
own: thanks all. will post canary dashboard link when live.
natalie: cheers. will close the loop here after first 2% run.
